home.title: My thoughts
home.emptyBody: When a thought bothers you, write it down here. We can look at it together, slowly.

step1.title: What's the thought?
step1.hint: Write it down the way it sounds in your head.
step1.placeholder: e.g. "I'm going to mess up the presentation."

step2.title: How much do you believe this thought right now?

step3.title: What does this thought bring you?
step3.hint: Even a painful thought can have a positive side, like protecting or motivating you. What does it give you, and what does it cost you?
step3.placeholder: Write what this thought brings you

step4.title: Look at the evidence
step4.hint: What supports the thought, and what doesn't? Rate how convincing each point is.

step5.title: Do you perceive some of these thinking patterns in your thought?
step5.hint: Tap a pattern to read more. Select the ones that fit, or none.

step6.title: Everything so far
step6.hint: Take a moment to read what you've written before looking for a more balanced view.

step7.title: A more balanced view
step7.hint: An alternative thought is a more balanced and realistic way of seeing the situation. It isn't about forcing yourself to think positively. It takes into account the evidence for and against, and the thinking patterns you noticed.
step7.help1: Looking at all the evidence, what is most likely true?
step7.help2: What would you say to a good friend who had this thought?
step7.help3: If you noticed a thinking pattern, how would the thought sound without it?
step7.alternativePlaceholder: What would be a more balanced way to see this?

step8.title: How much do you believe it now?
step8.rerate: How much do you believe the original thought now?
step8.alternativeBelief: How much do you believe the alternative thought? (optional)
step8.beliefChange: How much you believe the thought

complete.title: Well done
complete.body: You took the time to look at this thought from a different angle. That's real practice.

all_or_nothing.name: All-or-nothing thinking
all_or_nothing.description: Seeing things in black and white, with no middle ground.
all_or_nothing.example: "If it isn't perfect, it's a total failure."

overgeneralisation.name: Overgeneralisation
overgeneralisation.description: Taking one event as proof of a never-ending pattern.
overgeneralisation.example: "I got rejected again. This always happens to me."

mental_filter.name: Mental filter
mental_filter.description: Focusing on one negative detail and ignoring everything else.
mental_filter.example: "Someone frowned during my talk, so it went badly."

disqualifying_positive.name: Disqualifying the positive
disqualifying_positive.description: Dismissing good things as if they don't count.
disqualifying_positive.example: "They only said it was good to be nice."

mind_reading.name: Mind reading
mind_reading.description: Assuming you know what others think, without real evidence.
mind_reading.example: "She didn't reply, so she must be annoyed with me."

fortune_telling.name: Fortune telling
fortune_telling.description: Predicting that things will turn out badly, as if it were a fact.
fortune_telling.example: "I just know the interview will go wrong."

catastrophising.name: Catastrophising
catastrophising.example: "If I make a mistake, I'll lose my job and everything will fall apart."

magnification_minimisation.name: Magnification / minimisation
magnification_minimisation.description: Blowing up the negatives and shrinking the positives.
magnification_minimisation.example: "My mistake was huge; my success was just luck."

emotional_reasoning.name: Emotional reasoning
emotional_reasoning.description: Believing something is true because it feels true.
emotional_reasoning.example: "I feel useless, so I must be useless."

should_statements.name: "Should" statements
should_statements.description: Rigid rules about how you or others should, must or ought to be.

labelling.name: Labelling
labelling.description: Attaching a fixed, global label to yourself or others.

personalisation_blame.name: Personalisation / blame
personalisation_blame.description: Taking all the responsibility, or putting it all on someone else.
personalisation_blame.example: "The party was boring because of me."

reminders.notificationBody: If a thought is on your mind, you can write it down now. No pressure.

settings.privacyNote: Everything you write is stored only on this device.
settings.deleteAllBody: All thoughts and reminders will be permanently deleted from this device. This can't be undone.

page1.title: Hi, I'm here to help you slow down
page1.body: Some thoughts pop up automatically and feel very true. This app helps you write them down and look at them more closely.

page2.title: How a thought challenge works
page2.body: Write the thought, rate how much you believe it, look at the evidence for and against, spot thinking patterns, and find a more balanced view.

example.title: What a finished challenge looks like
example.body: Here's an example, so you know what's waiting for you. You'll also find it in your list of thoughts, and you can delete it whenever you like.

page3.title: Private and on your device
page3.body: There's no account. Everything you write stays on this device and is never sent anywhere.
page3.disclaimer: This app supports CBT practice. It does not replace a therapist or professional help.
page3.crisis: If you are in crisis or thinking about harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.

example.thought: EXAMPLE: I'm going to mess up the presentation tomorrow, and everyone will think I'm incompetent.
example.positive1: It pushes me to prepare well.
example.negative2: I feel so anxious that I avoid practising.
example.for1: I stumbled over my words in the last meeting.
example.for2: My heart races when I speak in front of people.
example.against1: My last presentations went well, and I got good feedback.
example.against2: I was asked to present because of my good work on the project.
example.against3: I've prepared the slides and practised twice.
example.alternative: I might be nervous and make small mistakes, but I've prepared well. One presentation doesn't decide whether I'm competent.

about.title: About the app
about.author: Hi! I'm a CBT patient myself, and I made this free and open-source app to help other people with their therapy.
about.contact: Questions or ideas? Write to me:
about.license: Free software, licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later.

what.question: What is a thought challenge?
what.answer: It's an exercise from CBT. You write down a thought that bothers you, rate how much you believe it, look at what it brings you and at the evidence for and against it, notice thinking patterns, and then write a more balanced thought. At the end you rate the original thought again to see whether anything has changed.

noAi.question: Why is there no AI in the app?
noAi.answer: Because you are supposed to do the thinking yourself. Looking for evidence, spotting patterns and finding a more balanced view with your own mind is what helps you learn to challenge your thoughts. When an AI does the thinking for you, it doesn't help with the therapeutic process.

example.question: What is the EXAMPLE thought in my list?
example.answer: It shows what a finished thought challenge can look like. It isn't yours, so you can delete it whenever you like.

belief.question: Why do I rate how much I believe a thought?
belief.answer: Rating the thought before and after the challenge helps you notice change. It's normal if the number only moves a little; even a small shift counts.

patterns.question: What are thinking patterns?
patterns.answer: Common ways our mind bends reality, like expecting the worst or assuming we know what others think. In CBT they're often called cognitive distortions. Spotting them makes it easier to step back from a thought.

privacy.question: Where are my thoughts stored?
privacy.answer: Only on this device. There's no account, no server and no cloud sync, and the app never sends what you write anywhere.

dictation.question: Does dictation send my voice anywhere?
dictation.answer: No. Dictation only uses your phone's on-device speech recognition. If that isn't available for your language, the microphone button is hidden. You can always type instead.

share.question: Can I share a thought with my therapist?
share.answer: Yes. Open a thought and tap the download button to save it as a Markdown file. Your phone's share sheet lets you choose where it goes; the app itself doesn't upload anything.

therapy.question: Can this app replace therapy?
therapy.answer: No. It supports CBT practice, but it doesn't replace a therapist or professional help. If you are in crisis, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.
